chunks: As for whatever is in it from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim al-Bajalī, I have narrated it from my father and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan—may Allah be pleased with them both—from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from al-Faḍl ibn ʿĀmir, and Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim al-Bajalī.

key_terms.أَبِي: my father; one of the author’s transmitting authorities
key_terms.الْفَضْلِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ: a narrator in the transmission chain
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I transmitted it; indicates direct authorial transmission of the report
key_terms.سَعْدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: a narrator in the transmission chain
key_terms.مُوسَى بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ الْبَجَلِيِّ: the named transmitter to whom this chain leads

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain to Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim al-Bajalī in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This passage provides the sanad/isnad through which the author transmits reports from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim al-Bajalī in the book. Its significance lies in documenting the route of transmission and preserving hadith attribution within Shia hadith scholarship.
